Let  
\[
M=\sum_{k=1}^{63} e(S_k),
\]
where \(S_k\) is the set of cells containing \(1,2,\dots,k\), and \(e(S_k)\) is the number of edges leaving \(S_k\).

For the \(8\times 8\) grid, the two checkerboard color classes each have:

- \(18\) interior cells of degree \(4\),
- \(12\) side non-corner cells of degree \(3\),
- \(2\) corner cells of degree \(2\).

Let \(s_r\) be the maximum possible edge-boundary of a set of \(r\le 32\) vertices. This is achieved by taking the \(r\) largest-degree vertices from one checkerboard color, so

\[
s_r=
\begin{cases}
4r, & 1\le r\le 18,\\
3r+18, & 19\le r\le 30,\\
110, & r=31,\\
112, & r=32.
\end{cases}
\]

For \(r>32\), the boundary is the same as the boundary of the complement, so the maximum boundary sizes are

\[
s_1,s_2,\dots,s_{32},s_{31},s_{30},\dots,s_1.
\]

Thus

\[
M_{\max}
= \sum_{r=1}^{32}s_r+\sum_{r=1}^{31}s_r
= 2\sum_{r=1}^{31}s_r+s_{32}.
\]

Compute:
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{18}4r=4\cdot \frac{18\cdot 19}{2}=684,
\]
\[
\sum_{r=19}^{30}(3r+18)
=3(19+\cdots+30)+18\cdot 12
=3\cdot 294+216=1098,
\]
and \(s_{31}=110\). Hence
\[
\sum_{r=1}^{31}s_r=684+1098+110=1892.
\]
Also \(s_{32}=112\), so
\[
M_{\max}=2(1892)+112=3896.
\]
